- When sentiment spikes (≥0.67) followed by a sharp drop, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment remains flat for 3+ days with low news volume, model often underestimates mean reversion — adjust upward by 0.3–0.8% per day until sentiment shifts.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment (≥1.0) with news volume ≥3, model frequently overpredicts 3–5 days later — apply a 1–2% downward correction on the 3rd–5th day of the spike.
- If model forecast is consistently 1–2% above true outcome over 3–5 days, it’s overconfident — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume drops below 1, model often undercorrects — add 0.2–0.5% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effects.
- If true outcome is consistently 0.5–1.5% below model for 5+ days, model is lagging — adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.7% per day to align with recent sentiment momentum.
